item.title: First Indiana bobcat season in 50 years ends after 250 harvested
item.description: The Indiana Department of Natural Resources has closed the bobcat trapping season after reaching the statewide quota of 250 bobcats in just four weeks, which was the first season since 1969.

item.title: Indiana legislation would toughen enforcement of immigration detainers, employee verification
item.description: A Senate panel advanced an immigration enforcement bill that requires state agencies to comply with immigration detainers and prohibits knowingly employing someone without legal status.

item.title: Eli Lilly to build $6 billion drug production facility in Alabama
item.description: Indianapolis-based Eli Lilly and Co. is investing $6 billion in a new active drug ingredient manufacturing facility in Huntsville, Alabama. The effort is designed to expand U.S. production and create 3,000 construction jobs and 450 permanent jobs.

item.title: Australia bans social media for under-16s, sets global precedent
item.description: Australia has become the first country to ban social media for children younger than 16, blocking access to 10 of the largest platforms including TikTok, YouTube and Instagram and Facebook. Many parents and child advocates welcomes the move, while major technology companies and free-speech advocates criticized the action.

item.title: Lamar Wilkerson’s record 44 points lead Indiana to 113-72 win over Penn State
item.description: Lamar Wilkerson set a career record with 10 three-pointers and 44 points as Indiana defeated Penn State 113-72.

item.title: 18-year-old faces charges in Thanksgiving Day murder and arson case
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS (WISH) — Prosecutors have charged a man for the Thanksgiving Day murder of two people in Indianapolis. Jaren Morgan, 18, was charged with murder, robbery and arson. item.title: Alison Krauss & Union Station featuring Jerry Douglas coming to Indiana in June
item.description: Alison Krauss & Union Station featuring Jerry Douglas will return to Indiana in 2026 with a stop at the Brown County Music Center on June 23 as part of their ARCADIA 2025 Tour.

item.title: Martin University to pause operations at end of year
item.description: Martin University in Indianapolis will pause its operations at the end of the current semester due to significant financial difficulties and a decrease in student enrollment.

item.title: Prospective citizens turned away at naturalization ceremony in Indianapolis
item.description: Marion County Clerk Kate Sweeney Bell condemned the turning away of prospective citizens based on their national origin at a naturalization ceremony in Indianapolis, calling for the federal government to reverse the policy and reschedule the ceremonies.

item.title: IMPD to roll out 10-hour shift pilot program starting Jan. 3
item.description: Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department will roll out a 10-hour shift pilot program starting Jan. 3, 2026, to address a shortage of 300 officers. Chief Chris Bailey said it will benefit the community because more officers will be on the streets during peak crime hours, and it will benefit the officers because they will have more time off.
